newsitem.title: UK: WORLD BONDS - JGBs braced for Tankan possibilities.
newsitem.headline: WORLD BONDS - JGBs braced for Tankan possibilities.

text.p: Japanese government bonds (JGBs) can maintain their overall positive stance unless the Tankan survey comes in far stronger than market expectations, analysts said on Tuesday.

The fourth quarter Tankan report, the key survey of Japanese corporate sentiment, is due at 2350 GMT on Tuesday. The market will be looking for any signs of acceleration in economic growth and indications of the Bank of Japan's future monetary policy.

"The general view now is that Tankan survey is not going to provide an opportunity for the Bank of Japan to raise interest rates," said Stuart Thomson, chief international economist at Nikko Europe in London. "The economy is still too weak."

"Even if the short term conditions of large manufacturing companies actually turn positive, and there is some negative market reaction, any weakness in the market will be seen as a buying opportunity," he said.
At 1203 GMT, December JGBs traded on LIFFE were at 125.30, unchanged from the close in Tokyo.

Analysts said trading activity in London would be subdued ahead of the publication of the survey, although covering of short positions had stimulated better than expected demand for the 2.8 percent 10-year JGB auction in Tokyo, pushing the market higher.

"Technically the market is positive which means there is an asymetric risk for the market to go up rather than down," said Alan Capper, bond strategist at Paribas Capital Markets in London. "Unless the Tankan is very strong you are more likely to see out of the market range trading or it'll start heading back up towards its previous highs at 126.52."
December JGBs touched a high at 126.52 on November 6.

"We're looking for short-term (market) weakness but nothing radically different," said Joanne Collins, economist at Nomura International in London. "We're still quite bearish on the medium-term outlook for the economy, and expect any major surge in growth for the foreseeable future."

She said Nomura forecasts were for the manufacturing index to come in at zero and for capital expenditure to grow 8.0 percent year-on-year, both at the higher end of market expectations, but these levels would not be a major issue for the market.
"It might trigger some buying of weakness and add to speculation about the timing of a rate hike," she said.
But analysts said the Bank of Japan was unlikely to raise interest rates until the middle of next year at the earliest.

"The improvement in business confidence we're seeing is as companies step up production to boost inventories ahead or the surge in demand in the first quarter," said Thomson. "That surge is prior to the 5.0 percent consumption tax hike. Once the tax is raised in April, demand will slump."

He said this, coupled with the problems in the financial sector, showed there was no opportunity for the Bank of Japan to raise interest rates, and without higher interest rates the impact of the Tankan survey was greatly reduced.
"If you get a very strong (Tankan) number it just might raise expectations of bigger rate hikes when they actually come, rather than sooner rate hikes," said Capper.
Forecasts for the next Tankan report due in February would also be a focus and could influence the strength of any market reaction to the actual fourth quarter data, analysts said.

"These are official forecasts so they give insights into what the Bank of Japan is thinking about for the future," said Collins. "But you've got to bear in mind that the Bank of Japan is always optimistic. While reasonably upbeat forecasts are likely to be a further negative for bonds, the market is somewhat sceptical."
